text:
maya: Heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s on hostedapi since 10:12 UTC. Heavy impact on chat and embeddings. Tickets piling up. :exclamation:
ops-bot: alert: svc=hostedapi severity=high route=/v1/chat /v1/embeddings spike_5xx detected at 2024-09-27T10:12:14Z
ken: on it. can you drop an example request and a trace id?
maya: sample curl from customer A:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
trace ids: trace=abc123:xyz, trace=def456:uvw (from X-Request-Id header)
maya: also seeing lots of client complaints about timeouts + slow retries -> billing hits too.
tara: rolled out auth-cache TTL change at 09:58 UTC to 30s (was 5m) to reduce stale creds. could be related. :thinking_face:
ken: that aligns. auth cache evictions at 10:11:xx show spike. if upstream auth backend slows, envoy can return 502 while waiting for token exchange.
support-engr: grabbing envoy logs for the frontdoor cluster now. quick grep showed repeated: "upstream reset before headers" and "stream reset" for same trace ids.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout auth-service v2 -> canary -> 2024-09-27T09:58:12Z by tara
ken: paste of relevant envoy snippet:
```
[2024-09-27T10:12:16Z] cluster=auth-backend upstream_reset reason=remote_reset id=abc123
[2024-09-27T10:12:17Z] stream_reset code=RST_STREAM upstream=pool-7
[2024-09-27T10:12:18Z] response_code=502 route=/v1/chat host=frontdoor-1
```
ken: root-cause hypothesis: auth-service canary + aggressive cache TTL caused auth cache thrashing -> upstream connection churn -> envoy 502/504s under short bursts.
maya: customers saw billing retries too — seems billing-service had elevated latencies and retried writes around same time. seen retry loops in billing logs.
sam: any mitigation we can do right now for customers?
ken: immediate mitigations: 1) revert auth-cache TTL change (rollback canary) 2) increase auth cache to 2m on frontdoor as temporary override 3) route high-priority customers to dedicated pool (if available) 4) add local short-circuit when auth backend latency > 200ms to serve cached tokens.
maya: rolling rollback of canary now. starting at 10:14:30 UTC.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback auth-service v2 -> in_progress by maya
tara: noted — will open a postmortem runbook item for cache TTL testing.
support-engr: creating follow-up ticket with traces, curl sample, and suggested mitigations. assigning to @ken for triage and @tara for deploy/process changes.
ken: will validate whether the billing retries amplified the auth backend load. likely a feedback loop.
maya: status update: after rollback we see 5xx rates trending down by 10:16:40 UTC. some residual 504s while connections drain. will monitor. :thumbsup:
sam: looping in account team to notify affected customers and credit if needed.
maya: next steps: (1) postmortem, (2) add pre-deploy load test for auth cache settings, (3) add automatic throttle for billing write retries when upstream latency high. I'll file the PM and link here.
ken: thanks. saving traces into support ticket. closing thread for now, will reopen if we see new spikes.
